subject: Acme POC - evaluation plan, success criteria, and eval methodology alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Acme POC - follow-up & draft evaluation plan

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have a shared plan going into the trial/POC: 

1) Success criteria (what you told us):
   - 90%+ accuracy on intent classification for priority intents (invoice_lookup, order_status, shipment_updates) measured on your dev dataset
   - 95th percentile latency under 250ms for single-user traffic pattern
   - Token cost target: <$0.004 per generated token average over the trial

2) Proposed evaluation plan (draft):
   - Week 0 (this week): finalize dataset and success criteria; Redwood provides POC workspace and baseline model configuration
   - Week 1: run offline evals on your sample dev set (metrics: intent accuracy, F1, hallucination rate)
   - Week 2: start online shadowing (non-blocking shadow traffic) for live metric correlation and latency profiling
   - Week 3: consolidation, final report, and go/no-go decision

3) Ownership:
   - Acme: provide labeled dev set + business owner for success criteria (Emily/Rajiv)
   - Redwood: run evals, provide dashboards, and manage infra/configuration (Marissa, Dylan)

4) Eval methodology question for alignment: offline evals vs online shadowing — we recommend doing both but want to confirm which you prefer as the primary gating signal for go/no-go. Offline gives faster iteration; shadowing validates production behavior.

5) Next steps from Acme: please confirm dataset delivery timeline (CSV export or shared Drive link) and whether the latency SLO above is realistic.

I've attached a first-pass evaluation plan and a one-page scoping sheet for your PMs.

Attachments: acme_eval_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 320 KB), acme_scoping_sheet_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48 KB)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20 min sync if that's easier.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the documents. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we can share a CSV export (anonymized) by Friday (2026-07-02). It contains ~12k conversational rows and labels for the 6 priority intents.
- Latency target: 250ms p95 seems reasonable for our typical queries; for some long-context flows we may accept slightly higher latency initially.
- Primary gating metric: Rajiv and I prefer offline intent accuracy + hallucination checks as the initial gate, then validate with shadowing before production.

Couple of asks:
- Can you add a short rubric for hallucination scoring (we want to be explicit about what counts as a hallucination vs. acceptable paraphrase)?
- Can Redwood provide an estimated token cost range for the baseline model versus the optimized quantized variant?

We can do a 30 min sync next week to finalize timelines — how's Tue 7/6 10:00am ET?

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme POC - follow-up & draft evaluation plan

Hi Emily / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of practical notes on evaluation methodology to align expectations: 

- Offline evals (what we run against your labeled dev set):
  - Metrics: intent precision/recall/F1, slot extraction exact match (where applicable), hallucination rate (we'll propose a simple binary label per response), and aggregated business-impact metrics (e.g., % of responses that would require human handoff).
  - Pros: fast iterations, reproducible, lower cost.
  - Cons: may miss latency/regression patterns seen under live traffic.

- Online shadowing (non-blocking):
  - We mirror a sample of live queries to Redwood without affecting customer experience, collect model outputs, and grade them offline (semi-automatic).
  - Pros: surface production distribution issues, real latency, and external data drift; good for validating offline results.
  - Cons: slower, needs sampling config and wire-up with your infra.

- Hallucination rubric (proposal — happy to refine):
  0 = Accurate: response contains only verifiable facts derived from prompt or dataset.
  1 = Acceptable paraphrase: minor rephrasing without introducing new facts.
  2 = Unsupported claim: response includes assertions not present in the input or knowledge base (counts as hallucination).

If that rubric works broadly, Redwood can label a 500-sample subset during Week 1 and report hallucination rate. We can also provide cost delta estimates for baseline vs quantized variant once we lock the baseline model.

Connor
Manager, Applied ML - Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme POC - follow-up & draft evaluation plan

Emily / team —

Quick operational notes and proposed ownership for the timeline you prefer (offline gating, then shadow):

- Deliverables & owners: 
  - Dataset ingest & schema validation (Acme) — Emily/Rajiv — due 2026-07-02
  - Baseline offline eval report (Redwood) — Connor — due 2026-07-09
  - Shadowing config + sampling run (Redwood + Acme) — Dylan & Acme infra — start 2026-07-10, run for 7 days
  - Final POC report & cost report (Redwood) — Marissa/Dylan — due 2026-07-24

- Metrics we'll include: intent F1, hallucination rate (per Connor's rubric), human-handoff %, average latency (p50/p95), and estimated token cost (avg & 95th).

- Cost estimates: Marissa/Dylan will provide a baseline vs quantized run estimate once we know the baseline model and avg token length. Expect ~30-45% token-cost reduction with the quantized variant in many workloads; we'll quantify for your dataset.

- Risk & mitigations: if offline and shadow disagree (e.g., good offline accuracy but high live hallucinations), we'll prioritize shadow for production decision and propose targeted prompt-engineering + caching to reduce regression risk.

I'll block 7/6 10:00am ET for a 30min sync; Marissa, can you send the calendar invite?

Thanks,
Dylan
